title: Report template
text:
Different Base R Styles

Enhanced ScatterHorizontal BarDonut-style Pie




Code
# Random data with grid
set.seed(789)
x <- runif(10, 1, 8)
y <- runif(10, 2, 9)

# Enhanced scatter plot
plot(x, y, 
     pch = 19, 
     col = "#296b7f", 
     cex = 2,
     main = "Enhanced Scatter Plot",
     xlab = "X values", 
     ylab = "Y values",
     xlim = c(0, 10),
     ylim = c(0, 10))
grid(col = "gray", lty = "dotted")













Code
# Data for horizontal bars
items <- c("Item A", "Item B", "Item C", "Item D")
counts <- c(15, 28, 22, 19)

# Horizontal barplot
barplot(counts, 
        names.arg = items,
        horiz = TRUE,
        col = "#7cc349",
        main = "Horizontal Bar Chart",
        xlab = "Count",
        border = "#528230")













Code
# Simple data
activity <- c("Coding", "Testing", "Documentation", "Meetings")
time <- c(40, 20, 25, 15)
colors <- c("#4e9db5", "#7cc349", "#ecba4c", "#19424e")

# Create pie chart
pie(time, 
    labels = paste(activity, "(", time, "%)", sep = ""), 
    col = colors,
    main = "Time Allocation",
    clockwise = TRUE)

title: Report template
text:
More Base R Variations

Line + PointsStacked BarMulti Pie




Code
# Time series style data
set.seed(999)
time <- 1:10
values <- cumsum(rnorm(10, 0.5, 1))

# Line plot with points
plot(time, values, 
     type = "b",
     pch = 16,
     col = "#296b7f",
     lwd = 2,
     main = "Trend Over Time",
     xlab = "Time Point",
     ylab = "Cumulative Value")













Code
# Matrix for stacked bars
data_matrix <- matrix(c(12, 8, 15, 
                       18, 12, 10, 
                       10, 15, 20), 
                     nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
colnames(data_matrix) <- c("Group A", "Group B", "Group C")
rownames(data_matrix) <- c("Category 1", "Category 2", "Category 3")

# Stacked barplot
barplot(data_matrix, 
        col = c("#4e9db5", "#7cc349", "#ecba4c"),
        main = "Stacked Bar Chart",
        xlab = "Groups",
        ylab = "Values",
        legend.text = TRUE)













Code
# Split plotting area for multiple pies
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# First pie
pie1 <- c(30, 70)
pie(pie1, 
    labels = c("Yes", "No"), 
    col = c("#7cc349", "#ecba4c"),
    main = "Survey A")

# Second pie  
pie2 <- c(45, 55)
pie(pie2, 
    labels = c("Pass", "Fail"), 
    col = c("#4e9db5", "#296b7f"),
    main = "Survey B")

title: quarto-fnl
text:
quarto-fnl 1.0.0
Themes for Quarto using FNL branding guidelines! This repository provides two theme extensions:

fnl: light and dark themes for HTML and revealjs formats.
fnl-report: light theme specifically for analysis reports in HTML formats.

View the documentation website for more details on usage and customization: https://ccbr.github.io/quarto-fnl/

title: FNL Themes for Quarto
text:
This is a Quarto template that assists you in creating a report, document, or presentation using the FNLCR branding guidelines.


To create a new document, use the following command:
quarto use template CCBR/quarto-fnl
This will install the extension and create an example qmd file that you can use as a starting place



You may also use this format with an existing Quarto project or document. From the quarto project or document directory, run the following command to install this format:
quarto add CCBR/quarto-fnl



To use the format, you can use the format names fnl-html, fnl-revealjs, or fnl-dashboard. For example:
quarto render report.qmd --to fnl-html
or in your document yaml or _quarto.yml file:
format:
  fnl-html


quarto add extension CCBR/quarto-fnl also installs a second, independent extension, fnl-report. It provides the fnl-report-html format for reports with a title banner, styled buttons, tab themes, author/affiliation cards, and table styles:
format:
  fnl-report-html
All assets are bundled with the extension, so documents render offline with no calls to Google Fonts or GitHub. Bundled assets include:

Roboto and Roboto Mono fonts
the banner image
the stylesheets

Button icons such as .btn-github and .btn-outline-email use Bootstrap Icons, which Quarto already includes in every HTML document, so there is no icon font to install or update. To add Font Awesome icons to your own text, install the fontawesome extension with quarto add quarto-ext/fontawesome and use its fa shortcode.
The report styles only load for fnl-report-html, so fnl-html, fnl-revealjs, and fnl-dashboard documents are unaffected.
See template-report.qmd for the available components, such as .btn-primary, .btn-outline-github, .panel-tabset .theme-ccbr-poppy, and .ccbr-footer.

The developers of this repository will update this section if any actively maintained versions of the software need to be publicly disclosed. Otherwise, contact the developers directly for any version information.

Locate the Report a vulnerability button. If the button is not on the Security and quality landing page, look under the Advisories section in the side bar.
